title: The New York Post Can’t Figure Out Why Pregnant Women Use Cannabis. Perhaps Because They Are Not Getting Adequate Medical Care?

content_html_sanitized:
To be clear, I have never recommended that anyone use medical THC, (CBD, yes), and most certainly not pregnant women.

 

However, an article in that internationally famous medical journal, AKA  the New York Post, explains “Why cannabis use is rising   among pregnant women — despite serious fetal risks…. Women are turning to marijuana to combat issues such as stress and anxiety, nausea, lack of sleep, vomiting, and pain.”

 

“Some may assume marijuana is safe for pregnant women because it’s legal in many states and because it’s a natural, plant-based product — but not all natural products are safe during pregnancy. For example, too much vitamin A can lead to birth defects, according to the American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG).”

 

If the Post is so concerned about babies, why is there not even a mention of fetal alcohol syndrome, which can be much worse than any possible consequences of cannabis use.

 

And alcohol is legal in every state, so why is the legal status of cannabis relevant here? Because it’s the New York Post.

See Of Course The New York Post Blames Minneapolis Shooting On Weed

 

Of course, one more bit of Prohibitionist propaganda from the Post really isn’t new or news, but there are actually two points of genuine concern buried in this organic pile.

 

The first is that problems in pregnancy, such as “morning sickness” are common and severe, but are clearly not being adequately addressed. Consequently, women are trying to selfmedicate and the antiemetic effects of cannabis are well known, at least outside of the medical community.

 

The failure of organized medicine to support even the sick and dying and severely disabled who find cannabis helpful is a betrayal of the Hippocratic Oath, and undermines their credibility generally.

See

The Wall Street Journal Carries Excellent Story About The Outrageous Medical Abuse of Veterans: But No Mention of Medical Cannabis

 

What kind of doctor would talk to the Post without reviewing the reporting of the contents? Is there really no safe level of cannabis use during pregnancy?

 

Some degree of nausea during pregnancy seems to be so common that it is not considered dangerous to either the mother or the baby.

 

However, some women suffer to such a degree that both the mother and the baby may have suffered from malnutrition during the pregnancy.

 

But here is how the Post reports it. “Several studies have shown that this exposure to cannabis decreases fetal weight, head circumference, and an increase in neonatal ICU admission,”

 

Really?

 

Question: Were these “studies” done only with children whose mothers had no complications during the pregnancy, such as severe nausea that caused them to use cannabis? Also, the poorer and less educated mothers may have other problems with substance abuse or bad dietary habits.

 

Correlation does not mean causation.

 

In any case, this is obviously not a new problem.
